explanation: A mutex (mutual exclusion) is a synchronization mechanism in C that allows only one thread to access a shared resource at a time, preventing race conditions and ensuring data integrity in multi-threaded programs. It is used to protect critical sections of code from concurrent access, avoiding issues like data corruption or double-free errors in scenarios involving shared data structures.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates mutex locking by having two threads (main and another) attempt to access a critical section. The main thread locks the mutex first, prints a message, and unlocks it. The second thread then locks, prints, and unlocks, showing that the mutex ensures only one thread executes the critical section at a time, thus preventing concurrent access issues.
